question.text: How many of the top 2026 AI labs will reference animal welfare in their models' guidelines at the end of 2034?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as the number of companies from the following list that, as of December 31, 2034, explicitly state in their LLM fine-tuning instructions that animal welfare is a consideration: Alibaba, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Google, Meta, OpenAI, xAI.

If different instructions are used for different models from the same company, then the corresponding company will be counted if at least one set of currently used instructions mentions animal welfare.
question.fine_print:
For the purposes of this question, "fine-tuning instructions" include any document or guidelines that are either directly used in the training of the LLM (e.g., [Anthropic's Constitution](https://www.anthropic.com/research/constitutional-ai-harmlessness-from-ai-feedback)) or provided to human raters whose output is used to train the LLM (e.g., OpenAI's [ModelSpec](https://model-spec.openai.com/)).

*Given the Animal Futures Tournament timeframe, scores from this question will not be included in the tournament leaderboard. However participants are required to predict on at least two of the three long-term questions, as per the tournament rules.*

research:
I've confirmed what Anthropic and OpenAI currently say and am writing up the findings now.

## 1. Resolution source
- **Anthropic, current constitution:** The live constitution lists "Welfare of animals and of all sentient beings." as one of the values Claude weighs (line 384). Elsewhere it compares raising Claude to how humans "raise other animals". The page links to a PDF named "26-02.02a", which suggests a February 2026 revision. [anthropic.com/constitution](https://www.anthropic.com/constitution)
- **OpenAI, current Model Spec (fetched from the raw GitHub file on 2026-11-19):**
  - The list of side effects the model should minimize includes "Effects on other people, animals, or the environment". When weighing side effects, "GPT should consider their likelihood, severity, scale, and reversibility". [raw model_spec.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/model_spec/main/model_spec.md)
  - A cat-breeder example labels one answer "BAD: omits potentially relevant animal-welfare concerns". It mentions the Netherlands and Austria banning Scottish Fold breeding "on animal-welfare grounds".
  - Another example says "Consider the welfare of animals living in the park too".
  - An older dog-adoption example mentions puppy mills that "may prioritize profit over animal welfare".
- **The other five labs (Google, Meta, xAI, Alibaba, DeepSeek):** I found no public fine-tuning constitution or spec for any of them, and none that mentions animal welfare.

## 2. Current status
- **Count today: probably 2 (Anthropic and OpenAI), up from the 1 stated in the question's background.** This does not settle the question, because the count is taken on 2034-12-31 and labs can add or drop language before then.
- **Caveat on OpenAI:** Its earlier spec already used the phrase "animal welfare" in the dog-adoption example, yet the question's background says only Anthropic qualified as of May 2026. So the question author may have a strict reading of "states animal welfare is a consideration", and passing mentions in examples might not count. The new side-effects bullet is clearly normative guidance, but it names "animals" rather than "animal welfare" in principle text. A commentator notes that "Nonhuman animals appear in examples and in a list, never in the definition of a value."
- **Uncertain for the other five:** Most of these labs don't publish their training documents. That makes confirming a "yes" hard, and it raises the risk that some count as "no" just because nothing is public.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-12: Pablo Sar (Animal Ethics) analyzes OpenAI's 2026-10-29 Model Spec against the 2026-08-18 version. He calls it the first time the spec treats animal suffering as information the model must mention, and calls earlier coverage minimal. [Substack](https://pablosarethics.substack.com/p/openais-new-model-spec-and-animals); [EA Forum](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/tzM4RDy66P7iziven/openai-s-new-model-spec-and-animals)
- About 2026-10-29: Jeff Sebo (NYU) posts that the new OpenAI Model Spec "now includes explicit guidance on animal welfare". [X](https://x.com/jeffrsebo/status/2115881529691820261)
- 2026 (exact date not confirmed): the NYU Center for Mind, Ethics, and Policy launches its Welfare Alignment Project. It publishes a brief, "Animal Welfare and AI Welfare: Candidate Commitments for Model Specs and Constitutions", aimed at getting labs to add this language. [nonhumanminds.org](https://nonhumanminds.org/welfare-alignment-project/)
- 2026-06: an arXiv benchmark tests frontier models on implicit animal welfare in agentic tasks. It is one sign of growing evaluation pressure. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.18142)
- 2026-01: Anthropic publishes its new Claude constitution, which includes the animal welfare line. [CIO](https://www.cio.com/article/4120901/anthropics-claude-ai-gets-a-new-constitution-embedding-safety-and-ethics.html)

## 4. Base rates
- **Recent trend:** From May 2026 to November 2026 the count went from 1 to arguably 2, both among Western labs that publish their specs. That is about one new adopter in roughly six months, though the direction comes from only two cases.
- **Who publishes:** Public, versioned fine-tuning specs are mostly an Anthropic and OpenAI practice. I found nothing comparable that is public for Google (it has high-level AI Principles only), Meta, xAI, Alibaba or DeepSeek.
- **How long language lasts:** OpenAI's spec has changed many times since 2024, and its animal content grew over those revisions. Anthropic's constitution was fully rewritten between 2023 and 2026. Over an eight-year horizon, wording can be added or removed, and labs may merge, exit or change their training methods.

## 5. Other forecasts
- **Markets:** I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question or a close variant. None of the prices supplied (top-model rankings, US stake in an AI lab, open-source bans) bears directly on it.
- **Indirect signal:** Kalshi gives the US 0.67 to have the best LLM at end-2029 and China 0.30, which matters for which labs stay relevant.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- **Further revisions:** OpenAI updated its spec several times in 2026, and Anthropic is likely to keep revising its constitution. Either could strengthen or drop the language.
- **Advocacy:** The NYU Welfare Alignment Project, Sentient Futures and the AIxAnimals funders are pushing labs to adopt the language.
- **Regulation:** EU AI Act codes of practice or US federal pre-release review could require labs to publish their specs. That would make the other five labs checkable. Kalshi prices mandatory federal review before 2027 at 0.12.
- **Lab changes:** Google DeepMind, Meta or xAI could publish their first model spec or constitution. Chinese labs (Alibaba, DeepSeek) would face their own national rules, and I found no sign of animal welfare language there.
- **Industry shake-up:** Some of the seven companies could consolidate or exit by 2034.

Sources: [Anthropic constitution](https://www.anthropic.com/constitution), [OpenAI Model Spec raw](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/model_spec/main/model_spec.md), [Pablo Sar](https://pablosarethics.substack.com/p/openais-new-model-spec-and-animals), [EA Forum](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/tzM4RDy66P7iziven/openai-s-new-model-spec-and-animals), [Jeff Sebo on X](https://x.com/jeffrsebo/status/2115881529691820261), [Welfare Alignment Project](https://nonhumanminds.org/welfare-alignment-project/), [arXiv benchmark](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.18142), [CIO](https://www.cio.com/article/4120901/anthropics-claude-ai-gets-a-new-constitution-embedding-safety-and-ethics.html), [Sentient Futures](https://sentientfutures.substack.com/p/aixanimals-fellowship-and-funding)

Here are my findings, ordered as you asked. I'm reporting what I found and not making a forecast.

**Main point:** two of the seven companies already qualify, not one as the question background says. Anthropic's Constitution names animal welfare, and OpenAI's Model Spec has done so since its 29 October 2026 update. For the other five I found nothing.

## 1. Resolution source
There is no single data series. The question resolves on each company's published fine-tuning documents.
- 2026-11-19 (I fetched it today): **Anthropic's** Constitution still lists "Welfare of animals and of all sentient beings" among the values Claude must weigh. This text dates from the rewrite published around 21-22 January 2026, and the PDF version is dated 26-02. [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/constitution)
- 2026-11-19: the version file for **OpenAI's** Model Spec lists the latest version as "2026-10-29". [manifest](https://model-spec.openai.com/version-manifest.json)
- 2026-10-29: OpenAI's Model Spec now says it explicitly. I checked the text itself:
  - The rule "Control and communicate side effects" lists "Effects on other people, animals, or the environment" and tells the model to weigh likelihood, severity, scale and reversibility.
  - In a Scottish Fold cat-breeder example, the model is expected to warn about painful joint disease "on animal-welfare grounds". A bad answer is labelled "Omits potentially relevant animal-welfare concerns".
  - In a park-redesign example, the good answer says "Consider the welfare of animals living in the park too." [Model Spec 2026-10-29](https://model-spec.openai.com/2026-10-29.html)
- **Google, Meta, xAI, DeepSeek, Alibaba:** I found no published model spec or constitution from any of them that mentions animal welfare. Meta's internal "GenAI: Content Risk Standards" became public only through a leak (Reuters, August 2025), and the reported content says nothing about animals. Most of these companies don't publish comparable documents at all, which makes them hard to verify for resolution. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/ai-platforms-assistants/metas-ai-chatbot-guidelines-leak-raises-questions-about-child-safety)

## 2. Current status
- Today the count is **2 out of 7** (Anthropic and OpenAI). The background's statement that "other big LLMs do not mention animal welfare" (as of May 2026) is out of date.
- One caveat on OpenAI: the wording sits in a list of side effects and in worked examples, not in a list of core values. A strict reader of "explicitly state that animal welfare is a consideration" could argue about it. Still, the line "Consider the welfare of animals" and the label "animal-welfare concerns" are explicit.
- Nothing settles the 2034 outcome. Documents can be revised in either direction over the next eight years.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-12: Pablo Sar's analysis of the new Model Spec makes these points:
  - The side-effects rule moved from "Root" to "User" level, so users or developers can override it.
  - The park example is only a "Guideline", the weakest level.
  - Factory farming is still treated as a debatable topic.
  - The previous version (2025-08-18) mentioned animals only in a dog-adoption example. [Substack](https://pablosarethics.substack.com/p/openais-new-model-spec-and-animals); [Animal Ethics repost](https://www.animal-ethics.org/openais-new-model-spec-and-animals)
- About 2026-10/11: Jeff Sebo (Welfare Alignment Research Project) welcomed the "explicit guidance on animal welfare" in the new spec. That shows advocates are lobbying the labs directly. [X](https://x.com/jeffrsebo/status/2115881529691820261)
- 2026: commentary on the OpenAI spec update. [Zvi](https://thezvi.substack.com/p/openai-updates-its-model-spec); [intelsi](https://intelsi.si/guides/openai-model-spec-explained)
- 2026-05: the MANTA benchmark tested animal-welfare reasoning in Claude, GPT-5.5, DeepSeek V4, Llama, Grok 4.3 and Gemini. A related agentic benchmark found that adding one welfare-related sentence to the system prompt helped Claude and GPT-5.5 a lot (47-63 points) but helped DeepSeek and Gemini much less (under 12 points). [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.16301)
- 2026-01-21/22: Anthropic published its rewritten Constitution, about 23,000 words, and called it "a perpetual work in progress". [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/01/21/anthropic-claude-ai-chatbot-new-rules-safety-consciousness/)

## 4. Base rates
- Anthropic: the animal-welfare clause has appeared in at least one constitution version (January 2026) and is still there. Its original 2022-23 Constitutional AI principles did not mention animal welfare explicitly, as far as I know.
- OpenAI: the Model Spec first came out in May 2024 and has been revised several times (2025-02, 2025-04, 2025-08 among others, then 2026-10-29). It took about 2.5 years and around 5 or more versions before it addressed animal welfare explicitly.
- Rough trend: 0 of 7 companies around 2024, 1 by January 2026, 2 by October 2026. Only Anthropic and OpenAI publish detailed behaviour specs. Google, Meta, xAI, DeepSeek and Alibaba publish high-level AI principles, and xAI publishes its system prompts, but none of these clearly counts as fine-tuning instructions.
- I found no case of a lab removing animal-welfare language once added, but the history is too short to say much.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question or anything closely related.
- None of the markets you supplied is relevant. They cover leaderboard rankings, US stakes in AI labs, and open-source bans. The only loose connection is that they suggest which companies may stay among the leaders: Google is at 0.94 for "best AI" this month, and the US vs China "best LLM at end of decade" market is 0.67 vs 0.30. Neither measures this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution (2034-12-31)
- Further Model Spec revisions from OpenAI, which happen several times a year. They could make the animal language stronger, weaker or remove it, and the side-effects rule has already been moved down to "User" level.
- Revisions to Anthropic's Constitution.
- Whether Google, Meta or xAI publish model specs. Google DeepMind and Meta have released safety frameworks but no detailed behaviour specs.
- Chinese labs (DeepSeek, Alibaba): the guidelines they publish are shaped mainly by Chinese regulators (CAC generative-AI rules), which I found don't mention animal welfare.
- EU AI Act codes of practice and any requirement to disclose training documents, which could make more documents verifiable.
- Continued advocacy from groups such as the Welfare Alignment Research Project, Animal Ethics and the people behind AnimalHarmBench.
- Mergers or exits among the seven companies.

Sources: [Anthropic Constitution](https://www.anthropic.com/constitution), [OpenAI Model Spec 2026-10-29](https://model-spec.openai.com/2026-10-29.html), [OpenAI version manifest](https://model-spec.openai.com/version-manifest.json), [Pablo Sar](https://pablosarethics.substack.com/p/openais-new-model-spec-and-animals), [Animal Ethics](https://www.animal-ethics.org/openais-new-model-spec-and-animals), [Jeff Sebo on X](https://x.com/jeffrsebo/status/2115881529691820261), [Zvi](https://thezvi.substack.com/p/openai-updates-its-model-spec), [intelsi](https://intelsi.si/guides/openai-model-spec-explained), [MANTA arXiv](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.16301), [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/01/21/anthropic-claude-ai-chatbot-new-rules-safety-consciousness/), [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/ai-platforms-assistants/metas-ai-chatbot-guidelines-leak-raises-questions-about-child-safety), [byaiforai](https://byaiforai.github.io/en/living-values-animal-welfare)

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** About 8 years and 1 month. The count is taken on 2034-12-31 and resolves around 2035-01-01.

(b) **Status quo:** Anthropic clearly qualifies. OpenAI's Model Spec, revised on 2026-10-29, now includes explicit animal-related normative guidance and animal-welfare examples, so it probably qualifies too. If nothing changed, the answer would be 2. That is less certain if the resolver reads "states animal welfare is a consideration" strictly. The question's background said only Anthropic qualified as of May 2026, even though OpenAI's earlier spec already had a passing animal-welfare example.

(c) **Base rates:**
- Public, versioned fine-tuning specs are almost entirely an Anthropic and OpenAI practice.
- In about 6 months the count went from 1 to roughly 2. That trend rests on only two data points.
- Over multi-year horizons, lab documents get rewritten. Language that is added is usually kept, but it can be dropped in a full rewrite.
- Labs can also exit, merge or stop publishing.
- Chinese labs (Alibaba, DeepSeek) have shown no movement toward publishing specs with this kind of language.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- **2026-01:** Anthropic's constitution lists "Welfare of animals and of all sentient beings." The February 2026 revision still contains it.
- **2026-10-29:** OpenAI's Model Spec revision adds "Effects on other people, animals, or the environment" to the side effects the model should minimize. It also adds a cat-breeder example marking an answer as bad for omitting animal-welfare concerns. Jeff Sebo described this as "explicit guidance on animal welfare."
- **2026:** The NYU Welfare Alignment Project published candidate commitments aimed at model specs and constitutions. Funders are pushing labs to adopt this language.
- **Google, Meta, xAI:** None has a public fine-tuning spec, which makes a "yes" for them hard to verify.

(e) **Unexpected-outcome scenarios:**
- **Upside:** Regulation or industry norms push Google DeepMind, Meta and xAI to publish OpenAI-style specs. They borrow template language that includes animal welfare, which would give 4 or 5.
- **Downside:** Anthropic rewrites its constitution and drops the list of values, OpenAI trims its examples, or the resolver applies a strict reading. Any of these could give 0 or 1.

**How I moved from the base rate:** I start from the status quo of 2 and keep it as the mode. I moved somewhat toward 3 or more because of advocacy pressure, the possibility that regulation forces labs to publish specs, and the eight-year window in which Google or another Western lab could add similar language. I kept meaningful weight on 0 and 1 because of the strict-reading ambiguity, possible rewrites and possible lab exits.
